title: Inputs are now snapshotted so the audit cannot be fooled by drift, and a second layer catches an answer of the wrong kind. Both layers still pass a wrong answer of the right kind -- demonstrated, not assumed.

built_1_input_snapshot.what: provenance.inputs records a sha256 and byte count for every file the argv names, taken at answer time.
built_1_input_snapshot.why: r48's stated limit: the auditor re-ran commands against the CURRENT filesystem, so a changed file flipped the verdict. That was the auditor blaming the skill for the auditor's own staleness.

built_2_shape_audit.what: audit_answer_shape(goal, result) compares the type the GOAL asks for against the type the answer IS.
built_2_shape_audit.why: r48's other stated limit: every audit answered 'is the answer derivable from its argv', never 'is that argv the right thing to run'.
built_2_shape_audit.the_demonstration: A skill taught honestly on 'unique lines of' was rewritten to claim the goal 'count the lines of' while keeping `sort -u`. Asked for a count it returned ['apple','zebra'] -- truth was 3. The derivation audit said ANSWER_MATCHES_ITS_SOURCE. The shape audit said SHAPE_MISMATCH__GOAL_ASKED_FOR_A_DIFFERENT_KIND, goal stdout_integer_value vs answer stdout_lines.
built_2_shape_audit.so: the two layers now disagree correctly, and the disagreement is information.

what_is_still_open_and_pinned.a_wrong_answer_of_the_right_type_passes_: 'count the unique lines' against a goal of 'count the lines' is an integer either way. No deterministic comparator can tell, and a test asserts this passes so nobody can claim it was closed.
what_is_still_open_and_pinned.the_audit_checks_DERIVATION_never_CHOICE: A confidently wrong argv that is internally consistent audits clean. Nothing here asks whether the command was the right one for the goal.
what_is_still_open_and_pinned.the_shape_audit_is_a_heuristic: it reads the goal's wording with the same 28/30 vocabulary. A goal phrased outside that vocabulary gets the wrong requested type and the shape audit becomes noise.
what_is_still_open_and_pinned.no_snapshot_of_the_world: only files the argv NAMES are hashed. A command whose output depends on anything else (locale, time, another process) is not covered.

the_2026_literature_says_this_is_the_kno.prefix_executability_arxiv_2610_40444: 'outcome-only and prefix-level rankings diverge: agents whose execution is conditioned on an unverified plan often achieve higher final success while substantially lowering executability.' Its deterministic prefix scorer checks tool existence, argument binding, type-compatible references, preconditions and benchmark acceptance -- no LLM judge.
the_2026_literature_says_this_is_the_kno.the_sentence_that_names_this_project: from the 2026 agent-evaluation reading: 'an agent might select the wrong tool, recover by accident, and still produce a correct answer. It would pass output-only evaluation, but you have now masked a systematic decision flaw that will surface under slightly different conditions.'
the_2026_literature_says_this_is_the_kno.the_layer_i_have_not_built: tool SELECTION correctness -- 'given the state and goal, did the agent choose the correct tool'. That is exactly the r48/r49 hole, it is a first-class 2026 metric, and this system has no measurement of it at all.

REAL: The audit now refuses to speak when its inputs have changed, instead of blaming the skill.
A wrong-kind answer is caught by a second layer (demonstrated on a rewritten skill).
23/23 answers still audit clean against snapshotted inputs.
Every prior result holds: 23/23 correctness, 28/30 typed heuristic on fresh phrasings, conflation probe clean, composition, environment shift, permanence.
NOT_REAL: That answers are verified. Two layers verify derivation and kind; neither verifies choice.
That the system can tell a right command from a wrong one that happens to fit the goal's type.
That this is replay. Inputs are hashed, not snapshotted for re-execution; a command depending on anything but a named file is uncovered.
That any of it reaches write, network, code execution, git: still refused.
That the arithmetic moved: 318 steps at 99% per step remains 4.09%. Still ZERO public-benchmark numbers.

the_sentience_claim: Unchanged. Two audit layers and a third still missing -- and the missing one is the one that would matter. Being able to check that an answer follows from its source is a property of a well-formed table. Being able to ask whether you chose the right action is a property of a system with a model of its own goals. This project has the first and demonstrably lacks the second: it will happily answer a counting question with a list and cannot notice.

the_smartest_things_to_do_next.1: Measure tool SELECTION correctness. It is the 2026 metric this project has never computed, it is the exact hole demonstrated this round, and it needs no new capability -- only a labelled expectation of which verb the goal implies.
the_smartest_things_to_do_next.2: Choose the contract from the goal at RECALL time as well as teach time, so a rewritten skill that claims a counting goal is refused rather than answered.
the_smartest_things_to_do_next.3: Add prefix-level executability: check each step against preconditions before running, not only after.
the_smartest_things_to_do_next.4: Still no writes. Every audit here depends on re-running the command; a write cannot be audited that way without doing it twice.

artifacts.changed: causal_trace_to_skill_compiler_v1.py -- _snapshot_inputs(), provenance.inputs, drift check in the audit, audit_answer_shape()
